title: John 14:15–31
context: If they love Him they will keep His commandments. He will ask the Father, who will give another Counselor, that he may be with them forever—the Spirit of truth, whom the world can’t receive. He will not leave them as orphans; He and the Father will make their home with the one who loves and keeps. The Helper will teach and remind. Peace He leaves; the prince of the world comes, and has no claim on Him. He does as the Father commanded so that the world may know He loves the Father, and as the Father commanded me, even so I do. Arise, let’s go.

voices.heading: Voices from both camps
voices.intro: How earlier teachers on both sides handled loving obedience and the other Helper, quoted directly.
voices.note: Quotations lightly abridged for length; wording follows standard English translations of the sources named.

arminian.quote: If ye love me, keep my commandments. I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever, even the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive. Peace I leave with you.
arminian.source: Explanatory Notes upon the New Testament (on John 14:15–17, 27)

reformed.quote: Love is the fountain of obedience. He will give you another Comforter: the Spirit is the bond by which Christ knits us to himself. The world cannot receive him, because it neither sees nor knows him. I leave you my peace.

verses.text: If you love me, keep my commandments.
verses.arminianNotes:
Love shows as keeping. The if is relational, not a wage scale.

This is a linkage. Grace that loves also keeps; claiming love without keeping is a contradiction He will not bless.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: love is the fountain of obedience. Future will keep describes love’s fruit.

Commandments flow from love He has already been forming, not from a loveless bargain.
verses.keyContrast: Love of Jesus keeps His commandments. Arminians underline the condition and enabled keeping. Reformed readers stress that keeping is love’s effectual fruit in those who are His.

verses.text: I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another Counselor, that he may be with you forever:
verses.arminianNotes:
He asks; the Father gives another Helper—forever, not a visit. Another means One like Jesus in advocacy, not a lesser deputy.

Classical Arminians: the Helper is promised to this believing company. Forever-with-you is covenant comfort; the wider world (v. 17) does not receive Him while remaining the world, yet the promise is for those who love and keep, a state people are called into.
verses.reformedNotes:
I will ask / He will give / another Helper / forever. The Father gives the disciples the Helper, a Trinitarian gift.

The Spirit is not a rental. This is Christ’s prayer answered in Pentecost permanence for His own.
verses.keyContrast: The Father gives another Helper, at the Son’s asking, to be with them forever. Arminians typically tie the gift to the loving, commandment-keeping community into which people may enter. Calvin’s heirs generally tie it to Christ’s effectual request for those the Father has given Him.

verses.text: the Spirit of truth, whom the world can’t receive, for it doesn’t see him and doesn’t know him. You know him, for he lives with you and will be in you.
verses.arminianNotes:
World cannot receive: not seeing, not knowing. You know: with you, will be in you. Two communities, one Spirit of truth.

Cannot receive is the world’s present blindness (3:3–8), not a ban on anyone ever coming. People leave “world” by new birth; the Spirit who will be in the Eleven also convicts the world (16:8).
verses.reformedNotes:
Cannot receive / neither sees nor knows. You know, because He lives with you and will be in you.

The world’s inability is not in doubt. The church’s knowing is already begun (with you) and about to be intensified (in you).

verses.text: I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you.
verses.arminianNotes:
Not orphans; I will come. Coming includes resurrection appearances and the Spirit’s making-Him-present.

Abandonment is refused. The going of 13:33 is not orphaning.
verses.reformedNotes:
Orphans refused. I will come to you: His own future tense.

The leaving is not the last structure of the relationship. He comes.

verses.text: Yet a little while, and the world will see me no more; but you will see me. Because I live, you will live also.
verses.arminianNotes:
The world will not see him, but the disciples will. Because I live, you will live—His life the cause of theirs.

Resurrection life is shared. The because is gospel; they live from His living, and are called to trust that.
verses.reformedNotes:
Because I live, you also will live. Union in life, not imitation only.

Their life is downstream of His. The world’s seeing ends; theirs does not.

verses.text: In that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.
verses.arminianNotes:
That day: knowledge of a triple indwelling—Son in Father, they in Him, He in them.

This is the Spirit-day’s lesson. Union is to be known, not only asserted.
verses.reformedNotes:
You will know: the day teaches coinherence.

Father-Son and Christ-church indwelling are revealed together. That day makes doctrine experiential.

verses.text: One who has my commandments and keeps them, that person is one who loves me. One who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him, and will reveal myself to him.”
verses.arminianNotes:
Whoever: keeping identifies the lover; then Father-love, Jesus-love, manifestation. Wesley would not split love from keeping.

This path is described so people may walk it. Manifestation is promised to the loving keeper, a conditioned experience of the risen Christ.
verses.reformedNotes:
Has and keeps: love’s evidence. Then the Father’s love, the Son’s love, and manifestation.

Manifestation is not a random mystic extra. It is pledged to the one whose love-keeping marks him as His.
verses.keyContrast: Keeping commandments marks love, and the lover is loved and given a manifestation of Jesus. Arminians catch a living condition. Reformed interpreters hear the described life of those Christ actually loves and indwells.

verses.text: Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, “Lord, what has happened that you are about to reveal yourself to us, and not to the world?”
verses.arminianNotes:
The other Judas asks the election-shaped question: why us, not the world? It is a fair question after 3:16 and 4:42.

The question keeps the world in view. Jesus’ answer (v. 23) will speak of home-making with the lover, not of a world God never sought.
verses.reformedNotes:
How… to us and not to the world: the manifestation is particular.

The Eleven are about to hear that love-and-keeping is the site of dwelling, which the world as world does not occupy.

verses.text: Jesus answered him, “If a man loves me, he will keep my word. My Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him.
verses.arminianNotes:
If anyone: not a closed caste slogan. Love, keep, Father loves, we come, we make home. The Trinity takes up residence.

Classical Arminians: anyone is the wideness inside the condition. The home is truly offered along the path of loving and keeping, which grace enables.
verses.reformedNotes:
If anyone loves: the home is with that person. We will come—Father and Son.

This is the answer to Judas’s how. Manifestation-not-to-the-world is home-making with the lover, a divine we.

verses.text: He who doesn’t love me doesn’t keep my words. The word which you hear isn’t mine, but the Father’s who sent me.
verses.arminianNotes:
Not-loving = not-keeping. The word they hear is the Father’s.

Refusal is locatable. One cannot claim the Father while binning the Son’s words.
verses.reformedNotes:
The heard word is the Sender’s. Not keeping is not loving.

Discarding Jesus’ words is discarding the Father. There is no higher appeal.

verses.text: “I have said these things to you while still living with you.
verses.arminianNotes:
Spoken while still with them: the earthly syllabus has a clock.

They must hold what He said in the flesh, because the Helper will remind, not replace, these things.
verses.reformedNotes:
While still living with you: the with-you season of speech.

The next verse is the other mode of the same teaching.

verses.text: But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you.
verses.arminianNotes:
Helper = Holy Spirit, Father-sent in the Son’s name, teaches all things, reminds of all Jesus said. Memory and teaching are His work.

He does not erase the spoken words; He reminds. The church still attends to what Jesus said, now tutored from inside.
verses.reformedNotes:
Father will send in my name. Teach and remind: two verbs, one canon of Jesus’ speech.

Reformed guarantee of apostolic memory: the Spirit is why they will not lose what He said. All things is all they need of His teaching, not a rival revelation.

verses.text: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
verses.arminianNotes:
Peace left and given, His, not as the world gives. The chapter’s opening command returns with fear named too.

Peace is given, then hearts are told not to be troubled. Receiving His peace is how the command becomes livable.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: I leave you my peace. World-peace is a different species.

This is a last-will verb, peace as His own. Troubled/afraid hearts are addressed by a gift, not a slogan.

verses.text: You heard how I told you, ‘I am going away, and I will come back to you.’ If you loved me, you would have rejoiced because I said ‘I am going to my Father;’ for the Father is greater than I.
verses.arminianNotes:
If you loved me, you would have rejoiced at His going to the greater Father. Greater here is the economy of mission (the sent Son returning), not a denial of 1:1.

Their grief is understandable and still too small. Loving Him includes wanting His glory with the Father.
verses.reformedNotes:
Father is greater than I: the sent one’s return to the Sender. Rejoicing would be love’s fit.

Reformed extra-Calvinisticum not required here: functional greatness of the Father as sender, while 14:9 still stands. They should rejoice at His exaltation.

verses.text: Now I have told you before it happens so that when it happens, you may believe.
verses.arminianNotes:
Told beforehand so that when it happens they may believe. Prediction is a faith-means.

He wants them to believe. The coming events are interpreted in advance as grounds for trust.
verses.reformedNotes:
Before it takes place / you may believe. Foretelling serves faith.

He scripts their future believing. The hour will not be raw chaos; it will be the thing He said.

verses.text: I will no more speak much with you, for the prince of the world comes, and he has nothing in me.
verses.arminianNotes:
Little talk left; the ruler is coming; he has no claim on Jesus. The devil’s hour is not a legal right over the Son.

Evil comes and finds no hook in Him. Their peace (v. 27) is that their Lord is not owned by that ruler.
verses.reformedNotes:
No claim: no hold, no debt, no sin for Satan to argue.

Reformed victory already in purity: the coming ruler meets a blameless Christ. The cross will look like Satan’s hour and be Satan’s judgment (16:11).

verses.text: But that the world may know that I love the Father, and as the Father commanded me, even so I do. Arise, let’s go from here.
verses.arminianNotes:
He does the Father’s command so the world may know He loves the Father. Then: rise, let us go—toward Gethsemane and the hour.

The world is meant to know. Obedience unto death is the Son’s love-language, and the going is already that obedience.
verses.reformedNotes:
So that the world may know: even the world is an intended audience of His love for the Father.

Rise, let us go. Teaching yields to the commanded path. Love of the Father is about to be visible in blood.
